title: noise-stitching-sprint-notes
content:
Sprint scratchpad — noise stitching / intermittent noise characterization

Goal:
- Understand and "stitch" intermittent latency noise that appears only when microbursts overlap with cold KV-cache misses. We want a lightweight analysis workflow to separate "real" tail events from sampling/collection noise and to propose mitigations (scheduling, batch thresholds, short-lived prefetch).

Hypothesis:
- Spikes are correlated with two independent factors: (A) short-lived cold KV cache misses (TTL priming) and (B) synchronous batching thresholds triggering at the same time at the worker. When they co-occur, p99 balloons ~3–8x.

Test setup (quick):
- Model: opus-6.7b-8q (quantized nightly build) pinned to v2025-07-08
- Sequence length: 256 tokens average (max 512)
- Host: g4dn.12x (8xA100-simulated env in perf rig), single worker per test node
- Runner: custom harness (runtest.py) that replays arrival traces; one-off vegeta checks for sanity
- Arrival patterns: baseline Poisson (λ=200 qps), injected microburst (2s pulse at +600 qps every 60s), and random sparse cold misses (TTL spray)
- Concurrency: 16 virtual clients (steady), target overall QPS variable per test
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, batch size distribution, kv-cache hit ratio, in-flight KV priming events

Commands I ran:
- python runtest.py --model=opus-6.7b-8q --seq=256 --trace=poisson+microburst.json --duration=10m --concurrency=16 --log=stitch-run-1.log
- vegeta attack -rate=200 -duration=2m | vegeta report -type='hist[0.5,0.9,0.95,0.99]'

Quick raw results (representative runs):
- Warm-cache baseline (no microburst): p50=42ms, p95=105ms, p99=245ms, qps=205, kv-hit=98%
- Microburst-only (cache warm): p50=46ms, p95=130ms, p99=310ms, qps=760 (2s window)
- Cold-spray-only (no microburst): p50=68ms, p95=220ms, p99=480ms, qps=160, kv-hit=78%
- Combined (microburst + cold-spray): p50=85ms, p95=390ms, p99=1.05s, qps=740 (during burst), kv-hit=60%

Simple ASCII heatmap (p99 across scenarios):
- baseline : [====      ] (245ms)
- microburst: [=====     ] (310ms)
- cold-spray: [========  ] (480ms)
- combined : [============] (1050ms)

Observations:
- p99 jumps disproportionately when cold misses and batch boundary align. The batch aggregator waits ~8–12ms to fill; if a cold priming request stalls KV read by 40–80ms, other requests in the same batch are held and see the stall (amplification).
- Batch sizes during combined runs show a bi-modal distribution: many small batches (1–3) and some large ones (8–16) that correlate with microburst arrivals. The large batches have the highest p99s when cold misses present.
- KV priming events are clustered (TTL spraying) and responsible for ~30–40% of the observed p99 in combined experiments.

Preliminary mitigation ideas tried (quick A/B):
1) Early release: if a batch waits >X ms (X=15ms) and contains a mix of 'fresh' and 'hot' requests, release hot ones with a partial result path. Result: reduced p99 by ~20%, but p95 slightly worse due to extra partial paths.
2) Preferential scheduling: prioritize requests with KV-hit=true into fast lane (bypass batch wait). Result: p99 reduced by ~30% on combined runs; complexity tradeoffs for fairness.
3) Prefetch priming: proactively prime nearby keys on microburst detection window. Result: reduced cold miss rate from 60%->42% in one test; operationally heavier (I/O spike).

Quick recommendations for next sprint:
- Build a small offline "stitcher" tool that ingests traces and attributes tail events to either batch amplification vs KV cold miss vs sampling artifact. Use moving-window causality (causal join on request_id timestamp and kv-read timestamps).
- Prototype preferential scheduling at the aggregator layer (short term flag) and test at 0.1 traffic fraction with canary. Measure fairness/tail tradeoffs.
- Add a lightweight metric: "batch-waited-ms" emitted per request so SLO decks can break down tail by waiting vs service time.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is there a cheap signal to classify a request as 'likely cold' before issuing KV read? (e.g., key-age heuristic from access logs)
- We should repro on Dedicated nodes (different isolation) — noise might be lessened but amplification still possible. Schedule a run on dedicated/dev cluster next week.
- Instrument the kernel path to see if OS scheduling or GC pauses are contributing to variance during large batches. I saw a couple 40–60ms GC spikes in logs but unclear correlation.

Next steps (short checklist):
- [ ] Implement stitcher prototype (python) and run on 3 recent traces (Marco will help)
- [ ] Canary preferential-scheduling flag on staging (Priya to coordinate)
- [ ] Add batch-waited-ms telemetry to request envelope (low overhead)
- [ ] Re-run combined scenarios on Dedicated node and compare

Conversation log pointers (practical):
- See GH:repo/perf-tests#312 for trace generator and trace file format
- JIRA INF-789: ticket tracking canary rollout for preferential-scheduling
- Confluence page for noise-stitching playbook (placeholder)

Notes: keep this doc intentionally informal. I want to preserve command snippets, quick numbers, and the brainstorming tone. Will flesh out the stitcher design once prototype exists.

— Izumi
